item.title: The Lex Humanitas Digitalis: Four Pillars
item.lead: The dossier proposes a model law that supplements existing regulations with explicit standards for digital intimacy services.

blocks.text: Pillar 1 is mandatory transparency in intimacy services. Ghost-chatting or substantial automation without clear notification would, according to the source, not merely be a matter of user experience, but a legally relevant infringement.

Pillar 2 is the limitation of psychological record-keeping beyond core functionality. The source aims to treat emotional or sexual CRM data more stringently when it is not essential for the provision of the service.

Pillar 3 is chain liability for digital management agencies. The principle is that not only the formal contracting party, but also parties that effectively exercise control over accounts, data, or labor can bear responsibility.

Pillar 4 is anti-fraud and AML audit on microtransactions when structural patterns or increased risk exist. The dossier thus aims to prevent the combination of many small payments from remaining undetected.
